decision: Product pages are static, revalidated on stock and price events
why: Shopping pages are read constantly and change rarely; events say exactly when to rebuild.
value: Fast first paint and SEO-friendly HTML without stale prices.

decision: Astro ships HTML first; only the search, bag and chrome hydrate
why: The editorial page is mostly content; hydrating it all would slow the hero for nothing.
value: The hero is interactive-free HTML, so it paints immediately.

decision: 'Describe a look' uses semantic retrieval filtered by size and nearby stock
why: People describe outcomes ('humid weekend'), not product names.
value: Results a customer can actually buy today, with a reason for each.

decision: Cards show pickup and stock from the customer's nearest store
why: 'Available' means nothing if it's in another city.
value: Pickup-today becomes a reason to buy, not a surprise at checkout.

decision: The stylist appears as a small suggestion, not a chat takeover
why: Most shoppers browse; AI should offer, not interrupt.
alternative: An open chat panel on arrival.
value: AI help is one tap away and never blocks the editorial.

decision: A stories rail for creators and the store floor, with gradient rings for unseen stories and gray once seen
why: People already read ring color as 'something new' from social apps; creator and in-store content converts better as a quick glance than as another grid.
alternative: A creator carousel of static cards.
value: New content is visible before the first scroll, and seen state is remembered per viewer only.

decision: The story viewer is a URL layer (?story=ninac): tap left/right, hold or press Pause to stop, arrow keys, product tags that open the PDP
why: The pattern is familiar from social apps; making it a URL layer means shareable links, Esc and focus handling come from the shared overlay stack.
alternative: A modal carousel held in component state.
value: A creator can share a link that opens their exact story; reduced motion turns auto-advance off.

decision: The billboard hero plays a muted CSS/SVG loop with a progress bar and a Pause control, the preview pattern popularized by streaming apps
why: Motion sells linen (it moves in the wind) but a video would cost megabytes and LCP; every animated part is transform-only.
value: The hero stays HTML and SVG with no media download, and anything that moves can be paused (WCAG 2.2.2).

decision: Row cards grow and reveal Add to bag, Save and sizes only after a 300 ms hover intent; keyboard focus expands immediately, touch shows actions inline
why: Row carousels with hover-expand (popularized by streaming apps) turn browsing into acting, but popping every card while the pointer sweeps is noise.
value: Quick actions without clutter, the same on mouse, keyboard and touch.

decision: Each row loads on its own (Continue shopping first) and swaps a same-size skeleton for content
why: Rows come from different services (history, recommendations, store stock); one slow service shouldn't hold the page, and matching skeletons avoid layout shift.
alternative: One page-level spinner until every row resolves.
value: The first row is useful sooner and CLS stays at zero.

decision: 'Pickup in 2 h near you' is filtered by the shopper's store and real ready-by times
why: Store stock is Maré's edge over pure online rivals; a row that promises a time must use the store's pick capacity, not just stock on hand.
value: The promise shown is the one Counter will actually keep.
